**Status:** `STABILIZED` Full V1 implementation.

## Bind one backend and one numerical policy

The operation ID is exactly
`scnsim.hb_response.josephsoncircuits.v1`. It transitively binds Julia `1.12.6`,
JosephsonCircuits `0.5.4`, General-registry tree
`43fa323200866910a93dd06ab8c002ed393ed9bb`, tagged source commit
`a88bafb8f57ad5b43ef302ae893288f0b75c11e3`, source conversion, lattice
construction, selected-network adaptation, artifact layout, and the fixed
controls below. V1 exposes no public HB numerics object or keyword.

Each request launches Julia with `--threads=1`, then calls and verifies
`BLAS.set_num_threads(1)` and `FFTW.set_num_threads(1)` before any case. The
observed counts enter attempt evidence. It calls the pinned backend with:

```text
iterations=1000
ftol=1e-8
switchofflinesearchtol=1e-5
alphamin=1e-4
nbatches=1
sorting=:none
keyedarrays=false
returnS=true
returnZ=true
returnSnoise=false
returnQE=false
returnCM=false
returnnodeflux=false
returnvoltage=false
returnnodefluxadjoint=false
returnvoltageadjoint=false
returnSsensitivity=false
returnZadjoint=false
returnZsensitivity=false
returnZsensitivityadjoint=false
sensitivitynames=String[]
symfreqvar=nothing
factorization=KLUfactorization()
```

The request supplies its exact `threewavemixing` and `fourwavemixing` booleans.
The controls, residual OR threshold, `nbatches`, and single-thread policy are
Human-approved Runtime Contract values. They are not caller-selectable
convergence knobs.

## Materialize one request-global lattice

Python validates pump axes, drive identities, case currents, truncation, and
trace modes. Julia materializes the finite ordered operating-point and
modulation lattices once for the request. For the pump lattice,
`odd=four_wave_mixing` and `even=three_wave_mixing`; for the modulation lattice,
`odd=three_wave_mixing` and `even=four_wave_mixing`. Enabling both keeps one
combined nonlinear balance and linearized response. Disabling both is an
explicit mixing-disabled request, not a different solver.

`max_intermodulation_order=N` maps identically to
`maxpumpintermodorder=N` and `maxmodulationintermodorder=N`; omission maps both
to `Inf`. `dc=true` exactly when any declared drive uses the all-zero tuple.
Pure DC uses `pump_axes=()` and `mode=()`.

For an operating-point tuple $m$, the lattice envelope stores the one signed
ordinary frequency $f_m=\sum_j m_j f_{p,j}$. For an input or output response
tuple, it instead stores the ordered grid

$$
f_{k,m}=f_k+\sum_j m_j f_{p,j},
$$

where `f_k` is `spec.frequencies[k]`; angular frequency is
$\omega_{k,m}=2\pi f_{k,m}$. Each response-mode grid has exactly the same
length and index order as `spec.frequencies` and the leading matrix dimension
$F$. This grid, rather than one representative sample, owns zero-frequency
preflight, the $W$ factors, mode permutation, and signed-grid reconciliation.

SCNSim preflights finite tuple lattices, tuple rank/order, every generated
conjugate, signed physical-frequency mappings and collisions, and trace modes.
A DC operating-point mode is legal. A zero-frequency linear-response channel
fails the complete request before an attempt because backend return-Z
normalization is singular there. Direct and HB frequency grids remain
independent.

## Convert drives without changing orientation

SCNSim uses `exp(-i omega t)` while JosephsonCircuits uses the conjugate phasor
convention. For a public coefficient $c_m$ at tuple $m$, the backend coefficient
at the same tuple is $c_m^*$ and the opposite tuple receives $c_m$; a DC
coefficient must be real and is unchanged. Port orientation is applied
separately. SCNSim materializes each conjugate pair before one backend lookup
and accumulates vector contributions in drive declaration order. The request
records every effective coefficient, tuple, injection map, and source-vector
artifact so no backend index becomes public authority.

## Solve each case independently and certify closure

Every case uses the original compiled nonlinear topology, including the full
Josephson sine rows. Mixing flags select lattice interactions; they do not
replace those rows with separate solvers. Cases execute in declaration order.
For every case SCNSim allocates a fresh

```text
zeros(ComplexF64, (Nnodes - 1) * Mp)
```

where `Mp` is the request-global operating-point mode count. There is no
cross-case warm start, state reuse, or continuation.

After the backend returns, SCNSim recomputes its pinned nonlinear residual
$F(x)$ at the returned $x$ because an upstream line-search warning or cached
residual is not success evidence. All $x$ and $F$ values must be finite. The
case closes only when

$$
\lVert F\rVert_\infty\le10^{-8}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\left(\lVert x\rVert_2>0\ \text{and}\
\frac{\lVert F\rVert_2}{\lVert x\rVert_2}<10^{-8}\right).
$$

The absolute comparison is non-strict and the relative comparison is strict.
Both residuals and the successful disjunct are evidence. Upstream warnings do
not waive this check. The verified public success outcome exposes this record
as `operating_point_closure`; the batch exposes the request-global loaded versus
response-linearization split as `topology_evidence`.

If a Ref contains PTC and any case has an effective DC or AC drive, preflight
rejects the request unless `allow_driven_ptc=True`. With that explicit approval,
the nonlinear/static balance still includes the original probe shunts. PTC
removes only proved probe loads from the response linearization at every
sideband. Evidence labels these separately as `loaded balance` and
`compensated analysis topology`; it never calls the operating point unloaded.

## Derive one selected network per case

The backend returns complete native S and return-Z. SCNSim first reorders both
by the same signed physical-frequency map, conjugates once, and applies the
frequency normalization

$$
Z_{\mathrm{native,phys}}^-=
W_{\mathrm{out}}
\left[\Pi_{\mathrm{out}}Z_{\mathrm{JC}}^+
\Pi_{\mathrm{in}}^T\right]^*
W_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1},
\qquad
W=\operatorname{diag}\sqrt{|\omega|},
$$

with the same map for native power-wave S. It does not reverse tuples a second
time. From that normalized native boundary SCNSim, in order, de-embeds all
backend source resistors, applies PTC per sideband, applies every
`transform_pair()` per sideband, retains/orders selected coordinates, adds
omitted matched loads, applies the selected source boundary, subtracts selected
source admittance, and derives public Y, Z, and matrix-reference power-wave S.
These are three surfaces of one selected network, not independent solves.
Every square normalization, de-embedding, Y-to-Z, and Y-to-S solve uses the
Runtime Contract's accepted normalized backward residual
$\eta(A,X,B)\le\tau(\operatorname{order}A)$. A finite native array with a
numerically unresolved solve becomes `HBCaseFailure(stage="response_formation")`.
A missing, nonfinite, or wrongly shaped native array is instead a request-level
`BackendProtocolError`.

Public matrices are stored exactly as `[F, C_out, C_in]` with axes
`(frequency, output_channel, input_channel)`. Channel labels are explicit
`(coordinate_id, mode_tuple)` pairs in coordinate-major/mode-minor order; flat
index is `coordinate_index * mode_count + mode_index`. `MatrixView.matrix`
exposes this three-dimensional stack without an implicit five-dimensional
reshape. Native S/Z use original logical-Port-major/mode-minor channels in the
same SCNSim signed-frequency order.

Reconciliation lifts an ordinary Port map as $Q\otimes I_{\mathrm{mode}}$ in
that flattened order. It is comparable only when topology, loads, PTC,
reference plane, reference matrix, signed frequencies, and normalization all
match. Otherwise the outcome records `comparable=False`, one closed reason
(`topology`, `load_or_ptc`, `reference_plane`, `reference_matrix`,
`signed_frequency_grid`, `channel_basis`, or `normalization`), and the SHA-256
identity of the longest canonical Ref-lineage prefix that remained comparable.
It does not fabricate a residual.

When it is comparable, `reconciliation.residual_f64` is only the normalized
per-frequency infinity residual of the backend-native-to-selected
reconstruction, with the maximum retained across the HB grid. It is diagnostic
evidence, not an acceptance or solver gate, and is never a Direct/HB comparison
residual. The record also carries the exact row-major physical-coordinate
projection and the identity of the Plan/View producer from which it came;
receipt verification reproduces the selected S matrix and residual from that
projection and the backend-native artifact. Different Direct and HB grids
remain independently declared and are shown side by side without interpolation.

## Normalize operating-point state evidence

Pinned JosephsonCircuits returns its fixed dimensionless reduced-flux solution
$x_{\mathrm{JC}}^+$ in a node-major/mode-minor vector. The call keeps
`returnnodeflux=false`: the SCNSim adapter reshapes that returned solution using
recorded backend indices, selects the request's representative pump tuples, and
derives

$$
\Phi^-_{m,n}=\varphi_0\,\operatorname{conj}(x_{\mathrm{JC},m,n}^+),
\qquad
\varphi_0=3.29105976\times10^{-16}\ \mathrm{Wb}.
$$

The adapter does not request, accept, or publish a second backend node-flux
output. The Result `states` surface is therefore nonlinear operating-point
evidence in SCNSim's `exp(-i omega t)` convention, not linearized signal
response and not raw backend $x$. It has shape `[Mp,Nn]`, axes
`(pump_mode,node_coordinate)`, mode-major/node-minor order, every compiled
non-ground node in compiler order, and unit `weber`. Evidence records tuples,
signed frequencies, backend normalization, and the real-signal relation
$\Phi^-_{-m}=\operatorname{conj}(\Phi^-_m)$; omitted conjugate partners are not
silently duplicated.

Every successful case also records one ordered `state_node_map` entry for each
column of the second `states` axis. Array position and `state_index` equal the
compiler node index, and `compiler_node_id` is that compiled node's exact
identity. The entry's closed `source` discriminator binds it back to sealed
topology:

| `source.kind` | Required sealed-topology binding |
|---|---|
| `plan_node` | `plan_node_id` names the exact Plan node and `visibility` is its exact `public` or `port_promoted` value. |
| `component_private` | segment-array `component_path` locates the frozen component snapshot and `private_node_id` names its exact private node. |
| `anonymous_internal` | `internal_node_id` is only the endpoint-derived `internal-<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>` audit identity. |

The map is provenance for interpreting operating-point evidence. It creates no
selectable state, `NetworkViewRef`, coordinate, or drive target; neither
`states` nor a map entry may be supplied to `retain()`, `transform_pair()`, or
`CurrentDrive.at`. Anonymous Internal nodes remain non-selectable.

## Seal exact case artifacts

Case ordinal text is `str(ordinal).zfill(6)` with natural growth after six
digits. Case IDs remain result identity and never enter paths. A successful
first case owns `artifacts/cases/000001/` with local artifact IDs and files:

| ID | File | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `s`, `y`, `z` | `s.zarr`, `y.zarr`, `z.zarr` | complete selected network |
| `backend_native_s`, `backend_native_z` | matching `.zarr` files | normalized original-backend boundary evidence |
| `states` | `states.zarr` | operating-point node-flux evidence in weber |
| `effective_source_vectors` | `effective_source_vectors.zarr` | exact accumulated physical drive vectors |

Each file has a same-basename `.manifest.json`. Every requested named trace is
a projection of selected S, never a second solve, and uses its declared trace
artifact beneath `traces/`. Matrix trees contain only paired `<f8` `real` and
`imag` datasets in C order. Selected/native matrices use
`[F,C_out,C_in]` and chunks `[min(F,1024),C_out,C_in]`; states and
`effective_source_vectors` use paired real/imag `[Mp,Nn]` arrays, axes
`(pump_mode,node_coordinate)`, and one complete-array chunk. Trace artifacts
use paired real/imag `[F]` arrays and chunks `[min(F,1024)]`. Units are:
selected/native S and traces `dimensionless`, selected Y `siemens`,
selected/native Z `ohm`, states `weber`, and effective source vectors
`ampere`. Matrix manifests carry their distinct selected/native channel lists.
The request-global frequency axis is
referenced from every matrix manifest rather than copied into each case.

An HB artifact link is deliberately case-local rather than globally named:

```json
{"case_id":"dc_pump","id":"s","path":"artifacts/cases/000002/s.zarr","sha256":"<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>"}
```

`case_id` plus local `id` supplies semantic role; the attempt-relative `path`
locates bytes only within the receipt-bound attempt; and `sha256` proves those
bytes. Local IDs such as `s`, `y`, `z`, and `states` may therefore repeat in
different cases. The ordered Result catalog carries each artifact's dtype,
shape, axes, units, and channel metadata; its manifest carries only the exact
regular-file tree and hashes. Both structures cross-check before receipt
sealing or `resolve()`, but neither infers meaning from a filesystem name or
array position.

A successful case must form complete selected S/Y/Z at every requested
frequency and publish the complete inventory above, its declared traces, all
manifests, channel/mode labels, ordered `state_node_map`, probe-load state,
convention, normalization, and hashes. A failed case has no `artifacts` member
or `state_node_map`, and its reserved ordinal directory must not exist. Raw
backend arrays remain evidence, not a competing public artifact.

## Keep every declared outcome consumable

Every declaration produces one `HBCaseOutcome` in order. A success exposes
S/Y/Z, traces, states, and evidence with `failure is None`. A numerical failure
stores an `HBCaseFailure`; accessing a success-only property rethrows that same
typed failure.

Failure ownership is exact:

| Condition | Owner |
|---|---|
| malformed request/lattice, zero response frequency, or missing driven-PTC approval | `SCNSimValidationError`; no attempt |
| unavailable Julia/package/thread runtime | `RuntimePreparationError`; no attempt |
| launch/process/envelope/version/source echo/mode order or purported-success shape/unit mismatch | attempt-backed `BackendProtocolError` |
| sealed compile topology breach | request-level `CompilerInvariantError` |
| nonlinear factorization/solve/final residual | `HBCaseFailure(stage="operating_point")` |
| linearized factorization/solve | `HBCaseFailure(stage="linearization")` |
| complete selected S/Y/Z numerical formation | `HBCaseFailure(stage="response_formation")` |
| artifact/schema/hash/receipt mismatch | `EvidenceIntegrityError` |

A Julia-detected numeric nonfinite response is a typed case failure; only a
purported success envelope containing missing, nonfinite, wrongly shaped, or
wrongly ordered arrays is a protocol failure. Reconciliation inequivalence is
`comparable=False`, not failure. Partial and all-numerical-failure batches are
completed reusable `HBBatchResult`s; request-level failures never masquerade
as case outcomes.

`hb.show()` plots successes and visibly lists every failure. Direct and HB keep
their native grids; presentation may overlay them but never interpolates or
infers a resonance. A finite lattice and local residual do not prove solution
uniqueness, stability, basin independence, or basis convergence. V1 provides
no warm-start branch control; the pinned backend's 3WM maturity remains an
explicit implementation risk, not another hidden failure threshold.
